findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted condition and wrong substring offsets
findings.body: In `isAccessTokenId`, the grant shortcut is extracted with `items[0].substring(3, 5)` but the encoded prefix is `<2 chars sessionType><2 chars tokenType><2 chars grantType>`, so the grant shortcut is at indices 4..6. Additionally the check is inverted: `if (items[0].substring(3,5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns false when the shortcut matches. Combined, the matcher accepts tokens with the wrong grant and can reject correct ones, so all event assertions using it (code-to-token, refresh, device, CIBA) do not actually verify the encoded grant type — the new feature is effectively untested.

findings.title: Null check for rawTokenId checks grantType instead
findings.body: The constructor calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` — it validates `grantType` twice and never validates `rawTokenId`. A null `rawTokenId` passes validation and later produces a token id ending in "null" or an NPE far from the source.

findings.title: Removal of public copy constructor OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context) breaks SPI consumers
findings.body: The `public Context(Context context)` copy constructor was deleted from the `OAuth2GrantType.Context` class in server-spi-private. Any custom grant-type provider or extension (this is a published SPI type) that subclasses or copies the context via this constructor will no longer compile/link. If the removal is intended, it should be deprecated first or at least noted as a breaking change in upgrade notes.

findings.title: Decoding an access token id with unknown shortcuts throws IllegalArgumentException
findings.body: `getTokenContextFromTokenId` throws `IllegalArgumentException` whenever the part before ':' is not exactly 6 chars or contains an unrecognized shortcut. Token ids are attacker/third-party controllable in endpoints that accept tokens (introspection, userinfo, revocation, logout, tokens issued by a differently configured/older cluster node or custom encoder). An unchecked exception there will surface as a 500 instead of an "invalid token" response. Decoding should fall back to the UNKNOWN context (as done for ids without ':') rather than throwing.
